children: New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- Banks in Gujarat are closed today, Saturday, 31 October, despite it being the fifth Saturday of the month. The closure is not related to the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) regular second- and fourth-Saturday bank holiday rule.

Instead, banks in the state are observing a special public holiday declared by the Gujarat government. The Gujarat government has included 31 October in its list of public holidays for banks in 2026. Here's why banks are closed in Gujarat today, whether branches in other states are operating, and what other bank holidays are scheduled in the state this year.
The Gujarat Government has issued a notification dated 27 November 2025, announcing the public holiday list for banks in the state for 2026.
The notification, numbered GS/22/2025/JSR/2025/509/GH, was issued under Section 25 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Ahmedabad.

The notification states, "The Government of Gujarat, in consultation with Reserve Bank of India, Ahmedabad is pleased to declare the following days to be public holidays for banks in Gujarat during the year 2026."
Under this list, 31 October has been declared a bank holiday on account of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary.

Therefore, bank branches across Gujarat, including those of the State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank, Punjab National Bank (PNB) and other public- and private-sector lenders, will remain closed today.

The fifth Saturday is ordinarily a working day for banks. Under the RBI's existing arrangement, banks observe holidays on the second and fourth Saturdays of every month. However, state-specific holidays can also lead to bank closures on other days.

Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was born on 31 October 1875 in Nadiad, Gujarat. Popularly known as the 'Iron Man of India', he was a prominent freedom fighter and India's first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister.

His birth anniversary is observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) to commemorate his contribution to national integration and unity. The Statue of Unity, the world's tallest statue, inaugurated in Gujarat in 2018, also honours his legacy.

According to the PM India website, Prime Minister Narendra Modi is on a two-day visit to Gujarat on 30 and 31 October. "On 31 October, at around 9 AM, Prime Minister will offer floral tributes at the Statue of Unity. Thereafter, at around 9:15 AM, he will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over Rs.400 crore in Ekta Nagar."

"Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday paid tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his birth anniversary, saying he dedicated his life to the creation of a strong, prosperous, and capable India," according to a DD News report today.
At around 5:30 PM, the Prime Minister will participate in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

No. October 31 is not a nationwide bank holiday. The closure applies to Gujarat under the state government's bank holiday notification. Therefore, bank branches in other states, including Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, and others, will operate as usual.
